plain_english: Nick's Stock Desk is a research screen for stocks. It does not place trades and it does not connect to a broker. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell.
The wheel page is a stock screen. The put and call walls page is market mood only. The Options page is education on debit spreads. It does not place a trade and it does not connect to a broker.

Each financial measure is +1, 0, or -1 versus that company's own recent history. Lower is better for forward P/E, trailing P/E, price/sales, debt/equity, and price/free cash flow. Higher is better for revenue growth, EPS growth, return on equity, and dividend yield. Analyst rating can be +2 to -2. Funds, insiders, the price trend, the oscillator, the latest earnings report, and the sector each add a small point. The score is the sum of the points we actually have.
A missing number is left blank and marked n/a. It is not stored as zero and it does not add or subtract a point. The freshness page counts the blanks.
Free data does not include a history of forward estimates. The baseline for forward P/E is the 3-year average of year-end trailing P/E. The column forward_pe_avg_basis says so.

The industry figure is the middle value of the other stocks in the same sector inside this desk's universe. It is not a paid industry database. If fewer than four peers have a number, the comparison is blank.

BUY, HOLD, and AVOID are research labels. A high score that is extended, in a downtrend, or missing most of its financials is labeled HOLD instead of BUY. Entry, stop, and target are a plan for study, not an order.

You will see an analyst target (median if we have it, otherwise the mean), a price/free-cash-flow target, a PEG-style target, and a blend of whichever of those exist. The trade target is separate: it is an entry-zone plan using the recent daily range.

Once a month the job asks what the score would have been using only data that was already public, then looks at the next 1, 4, and 12 weeks. Read the headline on the backtest page. If it says there is no clear edge, believe that. Past results are not future results. Delisted stocks are not in the test.

The 13F page is a summary: how many shares were increased versus decreased in the latest public holdings summary, plus a few of the largest holders. It is not a reprint of every fund, which is why the page stays fast. Insider points use open-market buy and sell counts from the last three months.

The put/call ratio is the CBOE equity ratio, with a 5-day average. Lines mark fear and greed. Option walls are open interest by strike for a short focus list, refreshed once a day. They are sentiment, not a trade.
AAII does not offer a free machine-readable survey. That page stays marked MISSING on purpose. We do not guess the number. Use the put/call page for a free mood gauge.

There is no free official daily S&P 500 earnings series this desk can rely on, and FRED is often blocked on the computer that updates the files. The historical P/E chart is the median trailing P/E of the stocks on this desk. The official column stays MISSING.
The macro page compares the latest published number with the forecast for a short list of US reports, then applies a simple, written-down map to each sector ETF. It is a sketch, not a forecast.

Prices keep the saved daily bars and ask Yahoo only for the new days, one or two chart calls at a time. Fundamentals, analyst ratings, 13F, insider counts, and option chains are fetched at most once a day and reused until the next session. If a source fails, the previous file is kept and the updates log says CACHED.

The desk keeps the daily prices it already saved and asks Yahoo only for the days since the last saved bar, plus a few days of overlap. Older bars stay put. A download that comes back short cannot erase a stock's history. If those overlap days do not match, which is what a split or a dividend adjustment looks like, that one stock is downloaded again in full. Once a week the after-close run downloads every symbol in full so the adjusted history stays honest. A symbol whose saved history is only a short stub, such as one cut down to a single day, is fetched in full once. Hourly runs do not do that weekly refresh. Turn features.incremental_prices off and every run downloads five years for every symbol and replaces the price file.

Every knob is in the incremental_prices block of config.json, and the on/off switch is features.incremental_prices. overlap_days (5) is how many calendar days before the last saved bar the next request starts. adjust_tolerance_pct (0.05) is a percent, and 0.05 means 0.05 percent, not 5 percent. adjust_tolerance_dollars (0.02) is 2 cents. A saved close mismatches when it moved by more than the wider of those two. The newest bar is left out of that check because it is still forming during the day. repair (on) and repair_below_bars (126) turn on the one-time full fetch for a short history. refresh (on), refresh_mode weekly, and refresh_every_days (7) redownload everyone on the after-close run when the last full refresh is at least 7 days old. refresh_mode slice instead redownloads one piece of the list each after-close run, refresh_slices (8) pieces, a different piece each day. chart_concurrency (2) is how many chart calls run at once. history_period (5y) is the length of a full download. The same wait-and-retry as the rest of the desk still applies after a refusal. backfill_per_run (40) is how many brand-new names a regular run downloads in full. fast_backfill_per_run (600) and fast_backfill_max_runs (4) belong to the catch-up. The switch for that is features.fast_history_backfill.

New names normally get five years of daily prices 40 stocks at a time on the regular 10:15 and 18:30 runs, so those runs stay inside an hour. features.fast_history_backfill is the catch-up switch, on until the new lists are filled in. While it is on, run Fill new price history from the Actions tab. That workflow downloads fast_backfill_per_run (600) names that have no saved bars yet, two chart calls at a time, the same five-year Yahoo chart the desk already uses. It does not ask for a profile, an analyst target, a filing, news, or options. Each run saves what it got. If names are still waiting it starts the next run by itself, at most fast_backfill_max_runs (4) runs. About 1,200 new names is two runs and about 1,200 chart calls. Turn the switch off when every new name has history. The regular runs keep using backfill_per_run (40) either way, and chart_concurrency stays 2.

The desk scores the S&P 500, the S&P MidCap 400, the S&P SmallCap 600, the Nasdaq-100, a short growth list, and other common stocks whose market cap is above $300 million, last sale is above $5, and screener volume is above 100,000, up to 2,500 names. A stock in more than one list appears once. index_membership shows SP500, SP400, SP600, NDX100, Growth, and Liquid together, so you can filter the page. Each list has an on/off switch in config.json. Your holdings and watchlist are always included. On a regular run, new names get a price history 40 at a time. To fill a large batch of new names the same night, use the fast history backfill.

Prices update twice on a New York trading day: once at 10:15 ET, which only fetches the new daily bars, and once at 18:30 ET, which is the full run (filings, profiles for the original list, 13F, and the close). The eight hourly runs from 11:15 to 17:15 are skipped while this is on. The keeper and the watchdog still make up a missed 10:15 or 18:30 by themselves. Turn features.twice_daily_schedule off and the eight hourly runs come back. The Trading Floor and the paper test still update on the 18:30 full run.

S&P 400 and S&P 600 come from the same kind of Wikipedia list as the S&P 500. indexes.sp400 and indexes.sp600 turn each list off. features.liquid_names adds common stocks with a market cap above liquid_names.min_market_cap ($300 million), a last sale above liquid_names.min_price ($5), and screener volume above liquid_names.min_volume (100,000) that are not already on those lists, stopping at liquid_names.max_stocks (2500). The Nasdaq Trader symbol files are used to skip ETFs, tests, funds, warrants, and preferred shares. Screener volume is the session volume in that feed, not a 30-day average. New names do not get a Yahoo profile, an analyst target, a forward P/E, a 13F line, or an insider count, because each of those would be another request per stock. A market cap is filled from the last price times the SEC share count when the profile does not have one. Company one-liners stay the hand-written file.

topic: SEC filings for the wider list
plain_english: A full run fills company facts for the whole universe, not 120 names at a time. It prefers the official nightly companyfacts.zip, and if that file cannot be used it asks for each company at under 8 requests a second. IFRS tags (Revenue, ProfitLoss, DilutedEarningsPerShare) are read for foreign 20-F and 40-F filers so names such as RY, MFC, and CCEP are not left blank. The older daily slice, sec_facts.batch_per_run (120) a day, is used only when sec_facts.full_universe is off. XOM is forced to CIK 0000034088 (Exxon Mobil Corporation). The ticker file points XOM at a different holdings company that has no yearly statements. HONA, SPCX, and VYLR are already the companies that own those tickers. They have not filed a 10-K, so the yearly columns stay blank and the quarterly columns fill in when a 10-Q is on file.

SEC submissions fill the company name, country, exchange, and SIC industry for the whole universe on a full run. SIC is mapped to an approximate GICS-style sector only where Wikipedia or Yahoo left sector or industry blank. Those SIC sectors are labeled sic_approx; they are not official GICS and they never overwrite a filled Wikipedia or Yahoo value. The Nasdaq earnings calendar is one request per weekday for the next earnings_calendar.days_ahead (60) calendar days, starting from today (the window moves into January on its own when the year changes). Next earnings is filled only where it is still missing. If a calendar request fails, the saved calendar is kept. Finnhub company websites run only when a FINNHUB_API_KEY is already in the environment; the desk never adds a key. A one-time Actions input, ownership_full, lifts the 13F and insider cap so every name in the universe is refreshed at the usual Nasdaq pace; regular runs still do 60 names. Company one-liners stay in the hand-written company_blurbs.csv file.

This page follows Nick's TradingView indicator: the 8-point trend template, the contraction count, the buy point, and the exit (7% stop, move to breakeven after 2.5 times the risk, sell part at 20%, trail a close under the 20-day average, climax warning at 25% in 10 days). A stock is listed only when the trend template is 8 of 8 and it has at least two tightening pullbacks, unless an open trade's buy printed at 8 of 8. READY means the green VCP tag (at least two tightening pullbacks) and price at or under the buy point. BROKEN OUT today means today's close crossed that point on at least 1.5 times the 50-day volume. WATCHING means 8 of 8 with at least two tightening pullbacks, but not ready: price over the buy point without that breakout today, or a trade still open from a buy made at 8 of 8. A name with only one pullback stays off the list, so it cannot be READY or BROKEN OUT and it never feeds Buy setups. vcp.min_pullbacks in config.json is 2. Set it to 1 to list those one-pullback names as WATCHING again. An open trade stays listed even if the score has dropped since the buy day, and the reason says so. An open trade is never READY: READY means not bought yet. If an open trade dips back under the buy point it stays WATCHING, and the reason says it dipped. Before a buy prints, the stop and target are the same percents measured from the buy point. The indicator itself waits for the breakout close. trend_score is written as '8 of 8' so a sheet does not read it as a date.

vcp.show_weaker_trend in config.json is off by default. Turn it on to bring back stocks whose trend template is under 8 of 8, labeled WATCHING (trend not 8/8) and listed last. They show on the VCP page and in the Chart Viewer (only when its include_watching is on). They never feed Buy setups, Leaders, or the sector rotation buy-setup share, because those read only READY and BROKEN OUT today.

C and A are the year-ago EPS change from the cached filings. N is how close the price is to its 52-week closing high. S is the 20-day average volume. L is the RS Rating, the desk's 1 to 99 rank of the past year against every stock it covers (MarketSmith style, not versus SPY), the same number as the RS column; l_rs_percentile keeps its old name and holds that number. A strict qualify needs RS 55 or higher and a soft watch 40 or higher. A stock with under a year of prices has no RS Rating, so it is not listed. I is the cached institutional increase versus decrease. M is SPY, and QQQ when that price is already on file, versus the 21, 50, and 200 day averages. A blank that says not verified was not in the cache. It is not a guess. This page does not set a stop or a target.

A box is a tight sideways range that closes out the top on above-average volume. A flag is a sharp rise, a short shallow pause, then a close above the pause on volume. Stop and target are the pattern levels described on the page. These two are desk rules. They are not the TradingView indicator.

A breakdown is the box turned over. The close is under the 50-day average, the 50-day is under the 200-day, and the 200-day is not rising. The base is a 20 to 60 day range that tightens, no wider than 10%. BROKEN DOWN today means the close is under that low on volume at least 1.4 times the 50-day average. WATCHING means the close is within 3% of that low, or under it without that volume. The chart shows the base low and a stop at the base high. The scan uses cached prices only.

Volume is how many shares changed hands. This page looks only at the daily prices and volume the desk already saves. Nothing extra is downloaded. Volume spike today: a stock traded at least 2 times its normal amount today (you can switch to 1.5, 3, or 5 times). Normal means the average of the 50 trading days before today. Up or down on volume: BUYING in green means the price closed higher on that big day. SELLING in red means it closed lower. Unusual volume streak: volume was above normal 3 or more days in a row. Quiet before a move: trading has gone very quiet (the last 10 days are under 0.6 times normal) while the price is within 5% of its 3-month high and above its 50-day average. Quiet spells like that sometimes come before a bigger move, up or down. During market hours today's volume is still adding up, so spikes look smaller until the close. Tap a row to see the price chart with volume bars and an amber line for the 50-day average volume. Research only. The switch is scanner_volume in config.json.

Education, not financial advice. The Options page lists a call debit spread for each of the first 15 buy setups, including names greyed by the market filter, and a put debit spread for the first 15 breakdowns, with BROKEN DOWN today first. Expiry is 45 to 60 days, or 30 to 75 when that is the only window. The long strike is about 0.55 to 0.65 delta. The short strike is about 0.30 delta, or the setup target when that price is closer to the stock. The debit has to be at most 40% of the width. A name is skipped for earnings before expiry, implied vol more than 1.3 times the 20-day realized vol, open interest under 500, a wide bid-ask, a stock under $10, or average volume under 1 million. Price Check compares the debit with a blend of 20-day and 60-day realized vol and at-the-money implied vol: CHEAP under 0.9, FAIR from 0.9 to 1.2, OVERPAYING above 1.2. Quotes are Cboe's free delayed feed, refreshed on a full run and around 10:30 and 3:30 ET, not every hour. If that feed fails, the last good quotes stay and the page shows their as-of time. Greeks are computed here. This desk never places a trade and it does not connect to a broker.

Qullamaggie's own rules: top 1 to 2% gainers, ADR of 3.5 to 5% or more, a 30 to 100% run in 1 to 3 months, then a 2 week to 2 month base with higher lows riding the 10 and 20-day averages (sometimes the 50). He buys the opening range high, puts the stop at the low of the day no wider than ADR, sells 1/3 to 1/2 after 3 to 5 days, moves the stop to breakeven, and trails the rest with the 10 or 20-day close. Daily-data approximations on this page: top 3% on the 21, 63 or 126-day return across the scanned stocks, a 30% run within the 63 days before the base that rose in 40 days or less, ADR as the 20-day average of high divided by low minus 1 (3.5% or more, 5% or more is tagged fast), price at least $20, a 10 to 40 day base whose second-half lowest low is at or above the first half, at least 70% of closes above the 20-day or all above the 50-day, and the 10-day above the 20-day with both rising. Desk rules with their own switches: base no deeper than 25%, base top within 10% of the run high, and the base starts in the top half of its range. The trigger is the day's high going above the base high when the prior day's high was not. Fill is the open or the base high, whichever is higher. Stop is that day's low. More than 1 ADR from fill to stop is Too wide, skip, and it stays on the page but not on Buy setups. 0.5 ADR or less is A+. ADR is used for this check on both pages. READY means the close is within 1 ADR under the base high. Volume of 1.5 times the prior 50 days is a ranking flag, not a rule. Volume drying up is shown as a flag. IN TRADE follows each breakout bar by bar: Sell 1/3 to 1/2 on day 3 to 5 with the stop at breakeven, then the first close under the 10-day ends it (qullamaggie.trail_use_sma20 switches to the 20-day). CLOSED shows the reason and the date, for up to 60 sessions. Market light (SPY and QQQ), results within 5 sessions, 20-day dollar volume, and shares for 0.5% risk of a $1,000,000 account are columns, not rules. Every rule has a switch in the qullamaggie block of config.json. Uses the saved daily prices only. No new download.

Marios Stamatoudis's own rules: ADR above 2.5% (he prefers 3.5%), opening range breakout entries, a stop at the low of the day under 1 ATR, partials at 2.5 to 3 ADRs above the entry (ADRs, not R), breakeven after the partial, and a trail on the 10, 20 or 50-day average. The slides that went around were Financial Wisdom TV's summary, not his own. This page uses the same daily-data base and entry checks as the Qullamaggie page, with ADR at least 2.5% (3.5% or more marked preferred), a prior run within 126 days, and the volume dry-up as a rule (last 5 base days under the 50-day average). The stop check uses ADR instead of ATR. A weak day-1 close (under the fill, or less than half the risk above it) is flagged. Selling: 1/4 to 1/3 when the high reaches the entry plus 2.5 ADRs (the 3 ADR level is shown too), then the stop moves to breakeven. A close under the 10-day sells 1/3 of the rest. A close under the 20-day sells the rest and the trade shows as CLOSED with the reason and date. Every rule has a switch in the marios block of config.json.

An Episodic Pivot (EP) is a stock that gaps up at least 10% on news, on at least 3 times its normal volume (Qullamaggie's and Stockbee's original rules). Gap is today's open versus yesterday's close. Normal volume is the 50-day average. During market hours the hourly runs judge volume by pace: volume so far versus the share of a normal day expected by that time, or a full normal day of volume already traded. That row is EP TODAY - FORMING. After the close, EP TODAY - CONFIRMED needs a close in the top half of the day and at or above the open. Otherwise it is EP FADED and is watched for a delayed EP for 20 sessions. DAY 2-5 WATCH waits for a move above the EP-day high, with the stop at the EP-day low. DELAYED EP WATCH (days 6 to 20) waits for a move above a tight 5-day range. A stop more than 1.5 times the normal daily range (ADR) is Too wide, skip. IN TRADE shows the plan: sell 1/3 to 1/2 on day 3 to 5, move the stop to breakeven, then sell the rest on the first close under the 10-day average (ADR 5% or more) or the 20-day. NO FOLLOW-THROUGH means it did not rise one normal day's move in 5 sessions (Stockbee's time stop): the best close since the fill is still under the fill plus 1 ADR. It is a flag only (episodic_pivot.time_stop_flag); the trade stays IN TRADE. CLOSED rows stay 10 sessions. Catalyst: an earnings report right before the gap (from the cached earnings dates), the EPS surprise, the last filed quarter's growth, and whether revenue growth sped up. Guidance, revenue beats, and non-earnings news cannot be checked on free data, so each row says to check the news. Market cap comes from the Yahoo profile the desk already downloads. Neglect grade A means flat or down for months before the gap, C means it already ran more than 30% in 3 months; it ranks, it does not filter. Nick's own filters are switches in the episodic_pivot block that start off, each with its number ready: gap of 10% or more, volume 3 times normal, price $5 or more, market cap $500M or more, 30-day average volume 500K or more, 3-month gain 30% or less, earnings only, catalyst score 2 or more, and neglect grade A. EP TODAY - CONFIRMED and DAY 2-5 WATCH rows feed Buy setups as READY, and a row that went above the EP-day high today feeds it as BROKEN OUT today. Too wide, faded and delayed rows stay out. No pre-market data and no opening range high: read that on your own chart. No new downloads.

The stock scorecard shows a CAN SLIM card for every stock: seven letters, each pass, fail, or no data yet. C is quarterly EPS growth of 25% or more versus the year-ago quarter. A is yearly EPS growth of 25% or more. N is a close within 15% of the 52-week closing high (the existing CANSLIM near-high line). S passes when the 20-day average volume is at least 200,000 shares and shows shares outstanding plus volume versus the 50-day average when those are on file. L is an RS Rating of 80 or higher (Nick; the CANSLIM scanner's strict qualify still uses 55). A stock with under a year of prices has no RS Rating and L shows no data yet. I is more institutional shares bought than sold in the cached 13F summary; missing 13F data is no data yet, not a fail. M is SPY in an uptrend: close above the 50-day and the 200-day, and the 50-day above the 200-day. A missing letter does not count as a pass or a fail. The switch is scorecard_canslim in config.json, separate from the CANSLIM scanner page. Research only. No new downloads.

RS is the desk's one RS score: a 1 to 99 RS Rating built the MarketSmith and William O'Neil way. It ranks how the stock's price did over the past year against every stock this desk covers, not against SPY. 99 is the strongest. 1 is the weakest. RS 85 means it beat 85% of stocks over the past year. The year is split into four quarters of 63 trading days, each its own block. The latest quarter counts double (40%). Each older quarter counts 20%. ETFs and funds are not stocks, so they are not ranked. Stocks with less than a full year of daily prices (253 closes) are left blank. The blank is not a zero. There is no partial-year score, so a new listing is not ranked against stocks that have all four quarters. It is worked out on every run from prices already saved. No new download. The RS column, the RS 70 filter, sorting, the Chart Viewer, CANSLIM's L, the scorecard L, Leaders, Highest EPS and RS, the Minervini screens, and Nick 360's RS Leaders all use this one number. rs_spy_3m (3-month return minus SPY, in the score and the Growth page) and the VCP page's rule 8 (the stock close divided by SPY, the same line as Nick's indicator) are separate checks and are unchanged. Turn the column and the filter off with feature.rs_rank. The scanners that need RS still use it. The numbers are in the relative_strength block of config.json.

Our copy of MarketSmith's Highest EPS and RS list (eps-rs.html). MarketSmith's own ratings are private, so these are close copies from the desk's own data. EPS Rating is 1 to 99: the latest quarter's EPS versus the same quarter a year ago, the quarter before that versus its year ago, and the yearly EPS growth rate over the longest span from 5 down to 3 years, each ranked across every stock on the desk with equal weight, then ranked again. EPS comes from the SEC EDGAR filings the desk already saves, split-adjusted. The latest quarter and the yearly growth are required. The quarter before counts when its year-ago quarter is saved (marketsmith_screens.require_prior_quarter turns on the strict three-part rule). Year-ago change is (now minus then) divided by the size of then, the same as CANSLIM's C. A stock missing a required part, or with a loss at the start of the yearly span, has no EPS Rating. It is blank, not zero. The list is desk stocks with EPS Rating and RS Rating both 80 or higher (marketsmith_screens.min_eps_rating and min_rs), ranked by the two added together, at most 50 (max_rows). Extended stocks are dropped: more than 5% over a VCP, Box, Flag, Qullamaggie or Marios buy point, or, with no buy point on file, more than 25% over the 50-day average as a stand-in (extended_past_pivot_pct and extended_above_sma50_pct). Saved data only. No new download and no paid data. Turn it off with feature.scanner_eps_rs.

Mark Minervini's trend template (minervini-1m.html and minervini-5m.html). All 8 rules must pass on the latest close, using simple moving averages: price above the 150 and 200-day, the 150-day above the 200-day, the 200-day higher than 21 trading days ago (1-Month) or 105 trading days ago (5-Month, about 5 months), the 50-day above the 150 and 200-day, price above the 50-day, at least 30% above the 52-week low, within 25% of the 52-week high, and RS Rating 70 or higher. The 52-week high and low use the last 252 daily highs and lows. Minervini calls the 1-Month list his heads up list and the 5-Month list his main list. Strongest RS first. The numbers are in the marketsmith_screens block. Saved data only. No new download. Turn them off with feature.scanner_minervini_1m and feature.scanner_minervini_5m.

Leaders puts a VCP that is ready or broken out today together with a strict CANSLIM qualify. A name on both uses the VCP buy point, stop, and target. A name on only one still shows, and any missing letter stays not verified.

The 52-week high is the highest intraday high of the last 252 trading sessions, and the 52-week low is the lowest intraday low. A new high today means the close is at or above the prior 252-session high. A new low today means the close is at or below the prior 252-session low. A stock can touch a new intraday high and still not count if it does not close there. Near the high means the close is within 5% of that high. That band is the zone Minervini prefers. A high on volume is a new high with volume at least 1.5 times the 50-day average. The page is research only. It does not place trades or send alerts. The count chart is built from the same cached daily bars.

Research list, not a recommendation. This desk never places trades. A stock is listed when VCP, Box, Flag, Qullamaggie, Marios, or CANSLIM is READY or BROKEN OUT today, or an Episodic Pivot is EP TODAY - CONFIRMED or DAY 2-5 WATCH, the verdict is BUY, the close is above the 50-day and the 200-day averages, and the risk from the entry to the stop is 8% or less. Qullamaggie, Marios, and EP rows marked Too wide, skip are left out. HOLD and AVOID stay off the list. The market filter, on by default, also requires SPY to be in an uptrend: the close above its 50-day and 200-day averages, and the 50-day above the 200-day. QQQ is shown the same way and does not decide the list. When SPY is not in an uptrend the list is empty and the page can still show those names greyed. Entry is the buy point of the strongest scanner that agrees. VCP uses the Minervini pivot. The stop is the tighter of 7% under the entry or the setup's own stop, and it is never above the entry. Target 1 is 20% above the entry, or 20% above the breakout close. Target 2 is the entry plus three times the dollar risk. Many breakouts fail, which is why the stop is always shown. No alerts are sent.

The graph compares the 11 SPDR sector ETFs with SPY using prices already in the cache. No new download. RS is the ETF close divided by SPY. RS-Ratio is 100 plus the z-score of that ratio, after a moving average, versus its own rolling mean. RS-Momentum is 100 plus the z-score of the change in RS-Ratio. Sample standard deviation, and a flat window scores 0 so the line sits at 100. 100 is the center and counts as the strong side. Leading is top right, Weakening bottom right, Lagging bottom left, Improving top left. Daily, weekly, and monthly use sector_rotation.windows (daily 10/40/5/40, weekly 6/26/4/26, monthly 3/12/2/12 for smooth, ratio window, change span, and momentum window). The score is 0 to 100. It blends 1, 3, and 6 month relative strength (21, 63, and 126 sessions, ETF return minus SPY, clipped from -15 to +15 points), the share of the sector's stocks above the 50-day and the 200-day, the share within 5% of a 252-session high, the share on a buy setup, the average desk score clipped from -4 to 12, the share of BUY verdicts, and a weekly quadrant bonus (Leading 100, Improving 70, Weakening 40, Lagging 15). A buy setup here is a name on the buy-setups list when that list is built. Otherwise it is READY or broken out today on VCP, box, flag, or CANSLIM, with verdict BUY and price above both averages. Weights are sector_rotation.weight.* and they are renormalized over the factors that exist. A missing factor is not a zero. The 10-year yield and the 10-year minus 2-year spread are the only macro series on file. Dollar, oil, and gold are not, so the page says they are missing. The tendency notes are general history, not a forecast. This page does not send a notification.

Under a stock's name, next to its chart, you will see one short line that says what the company does, like Makes iPhones and Macs and runs the App Store. These lines are written once and saved in data/company_blurbs.csv. They are not downloaded every hour. If a stock has no line, nothing is shown. The switch is company_blurbs in config.json.

Each scanner page starts with a short box called What this scanner does (or What this page does). It says in two or three plain sentences what the scanner looks for, why it matters, and how to use it. Pages with tabs add a This tab box that changes when you pick a tab. The switch is scanner_descriptions in config.json.

Edit input/holdings.csv and input/my_watchlist.csv to change the portfolio and the watchlist. Example rows are marked example=yes. Replace them with your own shares and cost. The desk still will not place a trade.

The desk updates on New York market time all year, Monday to Friday: every hour from 10:15 to 17:15 ET, plus the big evening update at 18:30 ET. In Pacific time that is 7:15 AM to 2:15 PM, and 3:30 PM, in summer and winter. GitHub sometimes skips or delays a scheduled update. A small watchdog checks four times an hour. If an update was due, none is running or waiting, and none started for that time slot, it starts exactly one make-up update of the same kind. It never adds extra runs, never retries a run that failed, and does not make up a slot more than 3 hours old. Some runs in the Actions list stop after a few seconds. That is on purpose: they are the clock-change twin of a real slot. The switch is self_heal_schedule in config.json. Turn it off and only the regular schedule runs.

GitHub's own timer sometimes skips scheduled updates for hours or days, so the desk keeps its own clock. One small keeper job is always running in the Actions tab (named Update keeper). It waits until 10 minutes after each update time (Monday to Friday, New York time, NYSE holidays skipped), checks whether that update ran, and if it did not, starts exactly that one update. 45 minutes after each update time it also checks that the update succeeded and that the prices reached that day (price_as_of in meta.json). If the update failed, it tries once more, and never more than once for the same time. If it succeeded but the prices are still old, it writes a warning in the keeper run in the Actions tab. It never starts a second update for a time that already ran, and never two within 50 minutes. A job can only live about 6 hours, so every 5.5 hours the keeper starts the next keeper and stops. Every regular update and watchdog run also starts a keeper if none is running, so a broken chain fixes itself. It downloads no market data and adds no Yahoo traffic. The switch is self_heal_keeper in config.json; the timings are in the keeper block (check_after_min 10, verify_after_min 45, recheck_min 15, chunk_min 330, min_gap_min 50, max_tries 2). Turn it off and the keeper stops at its next check and does not start another.

OK means the source answered and its columns have values. PARTIAL means a column is blank on every row. CACHED means this run failed and an older copy was used. MISSING means there is no copy at all. A blank cell is missing data. It is not a zero.

The sheet is filled by the Desk menu, not by IMPORTDATA. Desk > Refresh data now copies each file into the tab with the same name. Desk > Install hourly auto-refresh reloads about once an hour. The Setup tab shows the time of the last refresh. A blank cell means the number was missing. It is not a zero.

Gap Up lists stocks that opened above the previous day's high (a true gap, not just a high open inside yesterday's range) on any day in the last 21 trading days, today included. The gap must be at least 3%. Gap % is the open divided by the previous day's high, minus 1; the gap over the previous close is shown next to it. Gap-day volume must be at least 1.5 times the average of the 50 sessions before the gap day. The last close must be $5 or more, and the stock must trade at least $3 million a day on average over the last 50 sessions (close times volume, the same floor the Episodic Pivot scan uses), so thin stocks are skipped. Hold rule: no close since the gap day below the gap day's low. A close exactly at the low still holds. When a stock has more than one gap in the window, the newest one that still holds is shown. Rows are sorted newest gap first, then by the bigger gap. Columns: days ago, volume multiple, hold level (the gap-day low), last close, % above the hold level, where the last close sits in that day's range (0% is the low, 100% the high), above the 50-day and 200-day averages, and the other scanners the stock is on. Tap a row for the chart with the hold level, the gap-day high and open, the company line, and the reason. Gap Up does not feed Buy setups. Cached daily bars only. No new downloads.

Every Gap Up number has its own line in the gap_up block of config.json: lookback_days (21), true_gap_only (open above the previous high; off uses the previous close), min_gap_filter with min_gap_pct (3, a whole percent: the gap must be at least 3%; with the switch off any size counts), volume_filter with vol_mult (1.5) and vol_avg_days (50), price_floor with min_price ($5), liquidity_floor with liquidity_days (50) and min_dollar_volume ($3,000,000), hold_rule, skip_stale, sma_fast and sma_slow (50 and 200), and show_other_scanners. features.scanner_gap_up turns the page off. chart_viewer.include_gap_up puts the Gap Up list in the Chart Viewer and in All scanner stocks.

The Chart Viewer page shows one big chart at a time. Pick a list at the top: All scanner stocks (every stock on any scanner, once, with the stocks on the most scanners first), one scanner, Buy setups, or your watchlist. Tap Full screen, then swipe to the next chart. It uses the saved daily bars only. Nothing new is downloaded. Turn it off with features.chart_viewer in config.json.

Drag the chart with one finger to move it back and forward in time, and pinch to zoom in or out. To go to the next chart, flick quickly sideways: right for the next chart and left for the one before. A slow drag on the chart only moves it. A sideways swipe on the top row (the stock name, price, and counter) always changes the chart. On the button row it changes the chart only when all the buttons fit. The buttons wrap onto extra lines so they fit an iPhone without sticking out the side. If the button row is ever wider than the screen, a sideways swipe there scrolls the buttons and the chart stays put. The Swipe button swaps which way is next. The arrows on the sides and the left and right keys on a keyboard also work, and the counter shows where you are, like 3 of 120.

The Drag button next to Swipe picks what a one-finger drag on the chart does. Drag: move chart moves the chart so you can look at older days. Drag: next chart makes any sideways swipe change the chart, and the chart stays still. Your pick is saved on this device. chart_viewer.chart_touch_pan in config.json sets where it starts (on means move chart). chart_viewer.drag_mode_toggle shows or hides the button.

Each chart holds every day the desk has saved for that stock, about five years, so you can drag back to older days. Nothing new is downloaded. With chart_viewer.dense_default on, the chart opens at one candle width on every screen (chart_viewer.target_bar_spacing, 5.8 pixels), daily or weekly. Turn that switch off and it opens on the last 6 months of daily bars, or 3 months on a phone (chart_viewer.range_months and range_months_phone). A weekly chart then opens on the last 2 years, or 1 year on a phone (chart_viewer.range_months_weekly is 24 and range_months_weekly_phone is 12). The newest candle sits just left of the price scale, with the same small gap on every chart. Opening full screen or turning the screen puts that first view back, but if you dragged the chart, where you dragged to is kept when you turn the screen or open or close full screen. The 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All buttons are removed (chart_viewer.hide_range_chips is on). Turn that switch off to bring them back, and chart_viewer.range_chips can hide them again. Drag and pinch still move through the saved history. When a range is too long to fit, the chart shows as much as fits and keeps the newest candle in that same spot (chart_viewer.fit_wide_ranges, and chart_viewer.min_bar_spacing for the thinnest bars, 0.3 pixels). With the reason box back in the lower right, a long range keeps the newest candle just left of the box.

Every chart opens with the same thin candles, on a phone or an iPad, daily or weekly, light or dark. Each candle is 5.8 pixels wide, which is how an iPad daily chart looks in portrait (chart_viewer.target_bar_spacing). A narrow screen shows fewer candles and a wide screen shows more, and weekly candles are the same thickness as daily. The newest candle stays about 12 pixels left of the price scale. Candles never get thinner than 3 pixels (chart_viewer.min_bar_spacing_px), so a phone stays readable. If the stock has fewer bars than fit, they stop at 8 pixels wide (chart_viewer.max_bar_spacing_px) instead of stretching fat, and the empty space stays on the left. chart_viewer.dense_default is on. Turn it off to go back to 6 months, or 3 months on a phone, and 2 years of weekly bars, or 1 year on a phone. Drag and pinch still work.

topic: Chart Viewer lines and reason box
plain_english: The MA buttons turn the 10, 20, 50, 150, and 200 average lines on and off. On a daily chart those are days. On a weekly chart they are weeks, so MA 10 is 10 weeks. 50, 150, and 200 start on. Vol shows or hides the volume bars. The box at the top left of the chart lists every scanner the stock is on, its status, and a short reason. Tap it to read the full reason. Tap Why to hide or show the box. Your choices are saved on this device.

The Why box sits at the top left of the chart, where that corner is mostly empty, so the newest candle can sit just left of the price scale. It stays compact and does not cover the buttons, the Daily | Weekly switch, or the price scale. Tap it to read the full reason, the same as before. chart_viewer.why_box_top_left is on. Turn it off to put the box back in the lower right and leave room on the right for it again.

Daily | Weekly sits where the 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All buttons were. Daily is the start, and the pick is saved on this device. Weekly bars are built from the daily bars already on the chart. Nothing new is downloaded. A week is Monday to Friday. The open is the first open of that week, the high is the highest high, the low is the lowest low, the close is the last close, and the volume is the days added together. A week that has not finished yet still shows as a bar. The average lines use the bars on the chart, so on Weekly the MA 10 line is 10 weeks. chart_viewer.weekly_toggle shows the button. Off keeps every chart on daily candles.

Candles | Bars sits next to Daily | Weekly. Candles is the start, and the pick is saved on this device. It works on daily and on weekly. Bars are a vertical line from the high to the low, a tick to the left for the open, and a tick to the right for the close. Up bars are blue and down bars are pink, in dark mode and in light mode. The colors are chart_viewer.bar_up (#60a5fa) and chart_viewer.bar_down (#d946ef) in the dark, and chart_viewer.bar_up_light (#1d4ed8) and chart_viewer.bar_down_light (#a21caf) in the light. chart_viewer.bars_toggle shows the button. Off keeps every chart on candles.

Every Chart Viewer option has its own switch in the chart_viewer block of config.json: the list picker, full screen, full screen on iPhone and iPad (native_fullscreen_ios), swipes, how quick and how long a flick must be (swipe_max_ms, swipe_min_px), the swipe button, dragging the chart (chart_touch_pan) and the Drag button (drag_mode_toggle), the range buttons (range_chips) and hiding them (hide_range_chips), Daily | Weekly (weekly_toggle) with range_months_weekly and range_months_weekly_phone, Candles | Bars (bars_toggle) with bar_up, bar_down, bar_up_light, and bar_down_light, the opening candle width (dense_default, target_bar_spacing, min_bar_spacing_px, max_bar_spacing_px), filling the space when a range is too long to fit (fit_wide_ranges, min_bar_spacing), the arrows, the keys, the counter, loading the next chart early, each average line, volume, the reason box and its top-left spot (why_box_top_left), the company line, and the day change. include_watching adds stocks still forming a setup. include_closed adds finished trades. include_gap_up adds the Gap Up list and its stocks to All scanner stocks. include_trends adds the Trends list, Uptrend rows only, and its stocks to All technical stocks and All scanner stocks. group_toggle shows the Technical | Fundamental switch and default_group picks the side a device starts on.

topic: Chart Viewer on iPhone and iPad
plain_english: On an iPhone or iPad, Full screen fills the whole page instead of using Safari's own full screen, so Safari does not put its grey X over the stock name in the top left. Close it with the X on the right, or Esc on a keyboard. The chart stays clear of the notch, the rounded corners, and the home bar, standing up or turned sideways. Set chart_viewer.native_fullscreen_ios to true in config.json to go back to Safari's full screen. Computers always use the browser's full screen.

The Theme switch at the top of the left menu picks Dark, Light, or Match device. Match device follows your iPhone or iPad setting, so the desk turns light in the day and dark at night if your device does. Dark is the default. Your pick is saved on that device only. Every page, the Chart Viewer, and the charts change color; the numbers stay the same. On a phone, open the menu with the button at the top left. Hide the switch with features.light_mode in config.json; the desk then stays dark.

The left menu splits the screeners in two. Technical is for price and volume: VCP, Box breakout, Flag breakout, Qullamaggie, Marios, Episodic pivot, Gap Up, Minervini 1-Month, Minervini 5-Month, 52-week, 52-week breakouts, High volume, Pullbacks, Breakdowns, Trends, and Wheel. Fundamental is for the business and the desk score: CANSLIM, Leaders, Highest EPS and RS, Growth, Quality, Dividend, Stock scorecard, and Top stocks. Today, Buy setups, Trading Floor, Paper Test, Watchlist, Alerts, Backtest, Options, Earnings, Sentiment, Financials, Macro, and the market pages (under Market) are not screeners and stay where they were. Every scanner page keeps its own short description at the top. Turn the split off with features.split_tech_fund in config.json to get the old menu and Chart Viewer back.

topic: Chart Viewer Technical and Fundamental switch
plain_english: At the top of the Chart Viewer, Technical | Fundamental picks which side you look at. The list picker then shows only that side's lists, plus Buy setups and your watchlist. All technical stocks or All fundamental stocks is every stock on that side, once, with the stocks on the most of those scanners first. The box at the top left lists only that side's scanners; Buy setup and Watchlist lines show on both sides. Your pick is saved on this device and Technical is where a new device starts (chart_viewer.default_group). A link from a scanner page opens that scanner's side. chart_viewer.group_toggle hides the switch and brings back the single list with All scanner stocks.

The scanner_groups block in config.json says which side each screener page is on, by its page id: technical or fundamental. Any other word leaves that page where it was and out of both sides. The order there is the order in the menu. features.split_tech_fund turns the whole split on or off, chart_viewer.group_toggle shows the switch in the Chart Viewer, and chart_viewer.default_group is technical. Nothing new is downloaded.

The Trading Floor page is a short desk debate about today's top picks: the Buy setups list in its own order, topped up with stocks that are ready or broke out today on at least two pattern scanners, 15 stocks at most. Six roles each write one line. News says why it may be moving from fresh headlines (3 days). Scout compares today's volume with the 50 sessions before it, like the High volume page. Charts reads the entry, stop, and target the desk already worked out. Skeptic argues against the trade. Sentiment says whether the crowd is too hot. Each of those five gives +1, 0, or -1, and the Chief adds them up: 2 or more with no hard no from the Skeptic is BUY, 0 or 1 is WAIT, under 0 is SKIP, and a Charts veto (no usable levels, or the price already under the stop) is always SKIP. Tap a stock to see its chart with the entry, stop, and target lines. Research only: it never places an order, never calls a broker, and sends no alerts.

News: +1 when the fresh headlines that name the stock lean positive, -1 when they lean negative, 0 when mixed or when there are none (the line then says No fresh headlines found). Scout: +1 at 1.5 times normal volume on an up day, or 3 or more days in a row above normal; -1 at 1.5 times normal on a down day, or under 0.7 times normal; else 0. Charts: veto when there is no valid entry, stop, and target or the price is at or under the stop; +1 when reward/risk is at least 2 and the stop is 8% or less below the entry; else 0. Skeptic: one objection each for no fresh news, volume under 0.8 times normal, 10% or more over the 20-day average (or 25% over the 50-day), 5% or more over the entry, SPY not in an uptrend, and earnings within 7 days. No objections is +1, one is 0, two or more is -1; three or more, or 10% over the entry, is a hard no. Sentiment: one hot flag each for up 15% in 5 days, 8% over MA10, 12% over MA20, a 5% gap up today, 6 up days in a row, and 5 or more fresh headlines. No flags is +1, one is 0, two or more is -1. The full rules are in docs/trading_floor_rules.md.

News reuses the headlines the desk already stores for its focus list. Only picks with none of those get one request each to the free Google News RSS search (no key), on the after-close full run, once a day, so at most 15 requests a day and none on the hourly runs. Nothing extra is asked of Yahoo. The answers are kept in cache/trading_floor_news.csv for the hourly runs. A failed request is soft: that stock says No fresh headlines found and the Skeptic counts it.

features.trading_floor turns the page and its headline requests on or off. The trading_floor block in config.json holds every number: max_stocks, fill_from_scanners and fill_min_scanners, and one group each for news, scout, charts, skeptic, sentiment, and verdict. Each role has an on switch (off means it votes 0 and says Off in Settings) and each check has its own switch, such as trading_floor.skeptic.market_check or trading_floor.sentiment.gap_check. verdict.buy_min_total (2) and verdict.wait_min_total (0) are the Chief's cutoffs.

FAKE MONEY. The Paper Test page follows the Trading Floor's BUY calls with $10,000 of pretend cash, so you can see if the calls would have made or lost money. No real order is ever placed, no broker is connected, and no alert is sent. Each BUY call from the after-close full run waits one night and is bought at the next session's open, $1,000 each (10% of the starting cash), in fractional shares, with at most 10 open at once. A call is skipped when the stock is already held or waiting, or when there is no free slot or cash, and the page says why. The test started with the Nov 3, 2026 calls and only moves forward; nothing is replayed. The chart compares the fake account with putting the same $10,000 into SPY on the start day.

Stop and target 1 are the Trading Floor's, frozen on the day of the call. Each daily bar from the entry day on is checked in this order: opened at or under the stop, sold at the open; opened at or over target 1, sold at the open; touched both the stop and target 1 on the same day, counted as the stop to stay careful; touched the stop, sold at the stop; touched target 1, sold at target 1; after 20 trading days (the entry day is day 1), sold at that day's close. A stock that opens past its stop or target on the buy day is not bought. Win rate counts a closed trade with a gain as a win. Max drawdown is the biggest drop of the fake account from its own high. Rules: docs/trading_floor_paper_rules.md.

features.trading_floor_paper turns the page and the daily update on or off; off leaves the saved paper files as they are. The trading_floor_paper block in config.json holds start_cash (10000), position_pct (10), max_open (10), time_stop_days (20), fractional_shares (on), share_decimals (4), skip_if_held (on), and skip_gap_past_plan (on). The state is saved in data/paper_trades.csv, data/paper_equity.csv, and data/paper_summary.csv. Only the after-close full run changes them, and running the same day twice changes nothing. Hourly runs leave them alone.

Every price chart draws its moving averages in the same colors: MA 10 green, MA 20 orange, MA 50 blue, MA 150 yellow, and MA 200 red. That covers the Chart Viewer and the chart that opens under a row on the scanner and list pages, where SMA 50, SMA 150, and SMA 200 use the 50, 150, and 200 colors. The toggle chips and the values above the chart use the same colors. In light mode the shades are a little darker so every line shows on white. Change them in the chart_colors block of config.json: ma_colors for dark mode and ma_colors_light for light mode, one #RRGGBB color per average.

The Market news box on Today says why the whole market moved, not one stock. It shows S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow when the desk already has those day changes, one bold line from the desk numbers, and a plain line only when a free market-wrap headline lines up with those numbers. Headlines come from Reuters, AP, CNBC, MarketWatch, Yahoo Finance news, Investing.com, Nasdaq, BBC, The Guardian, the European Central Bank, and the Bank of England. Two or three short bullets and a row of sector chips show where the selling hit, or where the buying was. Up to five source headlines sit under The news behind the move. A short major-markets line names the verified index or ETF move for the US, Europe, the UK, Japan, mainland China, Hong Kong, and India when a real close is on file, and says unknown when it is not. More details stays closed and holds that table plus the cause tags, versus yesterday, breadth, the regime, the calendar, tips, the learning note, and the Friday week note. If no headline lines up with the desk numbers, the box says there is no clear cause and does not invent one. No alerts, no trades, no broker. The master switch is features.market_news in config.json.
When on, the card shows the bold reason, the plain source line, and the supporting bullets. When off, you get the short one-sentence line. Switch: features.market_news_why_detail (default on).

When on, The news behind the move shows up to 5 headlines, and any others sit in More details. When off, it shows 2. Big-picture feeds only, including major non-US macro when it can move markets. Switch: features.market_news_more_headlines (default on).

When on, Market news uses the Today card that stays balanced at 390px and 820px in both light and dark. When off, the same facts use a flatter layout. Switch: features.market_news_card_layout (default on).
When on, More details includes 2-3 research-only lines from the regime, breadth, and VIX. It never names a single stock and never places a trade. Switch: features.market_news_tips (default on).

When on, the card shows S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow with the day percent and a green or red arrow. Dow stays blank when the desk file has no Dow day change. Switch: features.market_news_indexes (default on).
When on, a row shows where the selling hit or where the buying was, using sector ETF day changes already on the desk. Switch: features.market_news_sectors (default on).
When on, More details is a collapsed row with the extra context. When off, that row is hidden. Switch: features.market_news_details (default on).
